scenes.headline: Delta Live Tables
scenes.subtitle: Declare pipelines; let DLT manage the rest
scenes.narration: Delta Live Tables lets you define pipelines declaratively while it handles orchestration, dependencies, and data quality.

scenes.headline: What DLT gives you
items: Declarative tables instead of manual orchestration
scenes.narration: You describe the tables you want and DLT figures out how to build them. It resolves dependencies and manages the execution graph automatically. Expectations let you enforce and monitor data quality inline.

scenes.headline: A DLT pipeline with expectations
scenes.narration: The @dlt.table decorator declares a managed table whose definition is a query. The @dlt.expect_or_drop expectation drops rows with a non-positive amount and records the metric. DLT builds this table, tracks its lineage, and keeps its data quality visible on the pipeline UI.

scenes.headline: How DLT runs
scenes.narration: You author table definitions and expectations in a notebook. DLT parses them into a dependency graph and orchestrates execution. It materializes the tables while continuously enforcing your quality rules.

scenes.headline: DLT vs hand-built pipelines
scenes.narration: Hand-built pipelines make you manage orchestration, retries, and checkpoints yourself. DLT handles all of that from your declarations and recovers automatically. Data quality becomes a first-class, built-in feature rather than scattered assertions.

scenes.text: With DLT you declare what you want; the framework manages how it runs.
scenes.narration: Focus on transformations and quality rules, and let DLT handle the plumbing.
